title: Lock a floating guide rod at the end of travel, where the carriage sets it
instruction: Lock the loose orange guide rod so the blue carriage runs the full length of the slide and back without sticking, show it with the crank, then let go.
context: Electromechanical equipment assemblers (O*NET 51-2023) and industrial machinery mechanics (49-9041) building a manual lead-screw slide leave its second guide rod loose, crank the carriage to the end of its travel and tighten the rod's clamp there, so the over-constrained rod pair lines itself up. Here the orange rod is pinned at the crank end, the preload spring in its floating end block pushes it 0.5 deg out, and the carriage's bushing has 0.3 mm of play. Locked as found, part-way along, or after the carriage has gone home, the rod stays skewed and the bushing binds. Unlike squaring a racked beam (TK-RWRT5A), setting a carriage preload (TK-ZEREPP), holding a sprung tensioner at its mark (TK-B5F4YZ) or drifting a plate into line (TK-K8D6ZZ), nothing holds the rod but the moving carriage, and the choice is where along its stroke to lock.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. Axis frame R: rod B's pivot at rod-centre height, world (0.350, 0.130, 0.7875). (1) Base: grey aluminium tooling plate 130 x 400 x 10 mm, 3.0 kg with its blocks, sRGB (0.72, 0.73, 0.75), fixed, centred at (0.310, 0.040), top at z 0.7575; on it dark grey steel end blocks (20 x 12 x 38 mm for rod A at y 0.144 and -0.094; 24 x 16 x 38 mm pivot block at (0.350, 0.130); 26 x 16 x 38 mm floating far clamp block at (0.350, -0.088) with an orange slot mark), a black 10 mm lead screw along y at x 0.310 from y 0.180 to -0.080 with an end bearing. (2) Rod A: steel guide rod, 8 mm x 250 mm, sRGB (0.62, 0.63, 0.66), fixed along y at x 0.270, z 0.7875, y 0.150 to -0.100. (3) Rod B: orange steel guide rod, 8 mm x 232 mm, 90 g, sRGB (0.95, 0.50, 0.10), along y at x 0.350, z 0.7875, y 0.136 to -0.096; pinned about a vertical axis at y 0.130; a preload spring in the floating end block (0.3 N m/rad) pushes its far end 2.0 mm outward against one side of the slot (+x, 0.5 deg); slot -1.0 to +1.0 deg; locked by the cam clamp (20,000 N m/rad). (4) Carriage: blue anodised aluminium, 0.40 kg, sRGB (0.15, 0.35, 0.85): a 110 x 30 x 8 mm plate over both rods (bottom 1 mm above them), a 24 x 40 x 18 mm linear-bearing housing on rod A, a 12 mm-long plain polymer bushing on rod B with 0.3 mm radial play (side walls 8.6 mm apart), a dark screw nut; friction 0.35 / 0.30; slides along y from the home stop (bushing B centre at y 0.106) to the far stop 160 mm on (y -0.054); starts at home. (5) Hand crank: black right-angle gearbox 40 x 40 x 50 mm, 0.8 kg, fixed at (0.310, 0.200), top at z 0.8075; on it a black crank turning about a vertical axis (20 mm hub, 55 mm arm, 60 g) with a black handle 14 mm x 34 mm tall (15 g, friction 1.0) spinning freely at 45 mm radius, starting at (0.355, 0.200); 32 mm of carriage travel per crank turn through the self-locking screw. (6) Cam clamp lever: red, 50 x 10 x 5 mm with a 14 x 12 x 8 mm grip, 20 g, sRGB (0.80, 0.10, 0.10), hinged along x on the far clamp block at (0.350, -0.092, 0.798); starts open 50 deg up (its free end toward -y), over-centre detents at open and flat. object_jitter 0.
scoring: Every control step from reset a whole-run record (a linkkit History, cleared only by the simulator reset) logs the carriage's place q along the rods, how far it trails its screw (lag), rod B's angle from parallel, the clamp, and each gripper's pad clearance and speed; every clamp closing starts a record of where the carriage has been since. Gate, any time in the run, gives 0: the carriage 1.5 mm or more behind (or ahead of) its screw for 0.15 s, i.e. stuck, or forced by hand. Ladder: 0.25 = the clamp is closed with rod B within 0.12 deg of parallel to rod A (0.47 mm over its length, a dial indicator at the far end); 0.5 = and since that clamp closed the carriage has been at the far stop (within 1 mm); 0.75 = and after that at the home stop; 1.0 = plus the release gate: every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the carriage, rod B, lever, crank and handle, and both grippers moving under 5 mm/s, for the last 1 s. Success (1.0) must hold 1 s. Real trial: a dial indicator on rod B's far end and a top photo of the lever; for the jam gate, a degree scale on the crank hub (5 deg marks, 0.44 mm of screw travel each) and a mm scale beside the carriage, filmed from above at 60 fps. Each frame the screw position is the crank angle times 32 mm per turn; a carriage mark 1.5 mm or more from it for 9 frames in a row (0.15 s) zeros the run, and the clutch's click (3 mm of slip) always lies past that gate.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Flip the red cam lever open (50 deg up), which frees rod B. Crank the carriage home to the left stop. Check rod B's far end rests against its preload spring 2.0 mm outward (a 2 mm feeler gauge against the slot mark), and leave the crank handle pointing forward (+x). The plate, rod A, the gearbox and the blocks are fixed on taped outlines and need no reset.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Rod B is a pinned link with a 0.3 N m/rad joint spring; the cam clamp is a stiff joint brake, on with the lever within 10 deg of flat. The lead screw is a 4,000 N/m drive whose target follows the crank at 32 mm per turn through a 3 mm (12 N) slip clutch; the crank feels no screw load. Rod A's bearing is the slide joint. Binding is PhysX contact on the bushing's 0.3 mm play (contact offset 0.5 mm, rest offset 0), as the clamp_as_found and clamp_mid runs show.
